# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 85 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 49 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_085_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 85

**1** Jesus said: "Adam came into existence from a great power and a great wealth, but he did not become worthy of you.

**2** For if he had been worthy, he would not have tasted death."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** A remarkable Thomasine statement: Adam, despite his exalted origins, is declared *less* worthy than the disciples who are addressed.

**"Great power and great wealth"** — Adam's endowments at creation are acknowledged; his failure is the greater because his starting position was high.

**"Tasted death"** — the idiomatic verb for experiencing death (cf. Heb 2:9; Mark 9:1; Thomas Saying 1 prologue). LOGOS's "experienced death" loses this specific idiom.

**"Worthy of you"** — *axios hymon*: the disciples are held up as the measure Adam failed to reach. This is the Thomasine reversal of the Adam-Christ typology: not "as in Adam all die" but "you surpass Adam."

---
